summary: Active Alberta cabin lookout on Willoughby Peak in the Crowsnest Pass, recorded as built in 1966; a blog lists it as abandoned, which the Alberta record contradicts.

facts.design: Cabin (Alberta record) with wood tower construction (OpenStreetMap)

staffing.as_of: 2022-06-06 (hiker wrote it did not seem to be manned)

access.note: Active lookout with buildings on the summit. Hikers use the trail; the 2022 hiker stayed away from the buildings. No source read says the public may enter them.

visit.trail_note: On foot from the York Creek staging area south of Coleman; a 2022 hiker's ascent took about 1 h 40 min.

facts.agency: Alberta Wildfire, within Agriculture and Forestry

events.note: Alberta wildfire lookout layer gives 1966 as the year constructed.

evidence.supports: location on Willoughby Peak in the Crowsnest Pass; south-west Alberta; blog calls it actively managed
evidence.quote: An actively managed fire lookout station on Willoughby Peak in the Crowsnest Pass (south-west Alberta).

evidence.supports: built 1966; cabin; 5 m tower height; elevation 2,078.5 m
blog list headed Abandoned Canadian Fire Lookouts includes Ironstone
each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.
June 6, 2022. A straightforward hike to a fire lookout.

evidence.supports: access via York Creek staging area south of Coleman
evidence.quote: Access is via the York Creek Staging area south of Coleman.

evidence.supports: hikers reach the lookout on foot, following the trail
evidence.quote: I followed the trail all the way to the lookout.

evidence.supports: did not seem to be manned that day; stayed away from the buildings
evidence.quote: It didn’t seem to be manned today. I stayed away from the buildings.

evidence.supports: bench named for Sarah Thompson, a former fire lookout
evidence.quote: Sarah Thompson was a former fire lookout and the bench is named for her.

evidence.supports: a local man gave the information to Bob Spirko (2015 ascent), not to the 2022 hiker
evidence.quote: Spirko got some information about this from a local man

evidence.supports: sign warns against shooting; trail nears a private residence
evidence.quote: The sign tells me not to shoot any guns and I'm nearing a private residence.

corrections.why: The Alberta record marks the lookout active (ACTIVE Y), and hikers reach it on a public trail. No source read says it is closed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A blog list headed Abandoned Canadian Fire Lookouts names Ironstone, but the same blog's Ironstone page calls it an actively managed station and the Alberta record marks it active. Treated as active.

sources.title: Alberta wildfire lookout layer (friaa_firesmart_vector_data), attribute query for three sites

notes_for_editor: Two sources contradict each other on whether the lookout is abandoned (blog list vs blog's own page and the Alberta record). The Alberta record is treated as authoritative. The only site-specific staffing evidence is one visit in June 2022. Possible duplicate: data/research/ca-ab-ironstone.json describes a lookout on Willoughby Ridge in the Crowsnest Pass, says no build date was found (the Alberta layer gives 1966), and calls it a watch tower where the layer says cabin. Check whether the two records are the same site before publishing.
